utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know, and I don't know how I could have supported it, because it was part of my brigade. And I have made a reference to the first decision taken by the Supreme Court of Republika Srpska where the status of volunteers was clarified, and this unit was a -- the commanders, the very commander's unit, and they were from the same part from where the commander was, but they had ideological differences with the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: May we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me try this. Mr. Dunjic, do you agree this is a report by General Galic? Shall we show him the second page. Colonel Galic and back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not question it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In para 3 he refers to a certain group commanded by Branislav Gavrilovic. Is he the same Gavrilovic you referred to in your paragraph 13 who was allegedly under your command at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is the same person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then can you explain us how -- why you say that they didn't commit any crimes, how come the commander of SRK is referring to him as leader of a group of criminals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know what the corps commander meant by this, but as I've already said, I had no evidence, nor did the corps commander provide in this report any evidence that any crimes had been committed so that I could take action other than generalised assessments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. West, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one thing in the transcript. It's not stated clearly in the transcript that the witness said that that unit, starting with the commander all the way down to the plain soldiers, they were the local population, but ideologically they were affiliated with Seselj. They did not just come there. And that is not clearly reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you confirm having said that, Mr. Dunjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. 65 ter 09365, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And just to back up for a moment, you say that "they were" -- "they were the local population, but ideologically they were affiliated with Seselj." This unit was affiliated with Seselj? Brne's unit?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: You cannot say affiliated with Seselj. Ideologically they were affiliated. It wasn't that it was Seselj's unit while I was commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So we have a December 16th document from 1992, and this is during the time where you had spoken earlier about being in the area of Zuc. This is a report, a corps command report from Kosovac, and he speaks about what happened at Zuc, and as we know from your testimony and a previous witness, we understand in December that the ABiH took control of Zuc. And at the third paragraph he speaks about it being basically a mess. And then in the fourth paragraph he says: "In the territory of municipalities, Hadzici, Ilidza, Rajlovac and Vogosca, the main organiser of paramilitary formations is Major Dunjic, commander of the Ilidza Brigade." Now you're going to see this in B/C/S. And we've got the English. Now, I can represent to the Court if you go to the B/C/S, Dunjic is pronounced -- excuse me, spelled correctly. And also if you go to the B/C/S, it says the commander of the Blazuski Brigade. So your headquarters were located in Blazuj; right?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So this Dunjic of whom they speak here, they're speaking about you; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And do you deny that you were the main organiser -- organisers of the paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: I absolute deny that. And could you please tell me who it was that signed this document? Because you said that this is a report of the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. If you heard that I misspoke. I said it was Colonel Kosovac, who was assistant for commander moral affairs. But if we continue on in this document I think you'll remember who Kosovac was. It then goes on to say his position, meaning you, of the brigade commander is a formality because he does not come to the brigade for three days. He put under his command paramilitary formations and some special units. He supplies them with the arms and munitions. He took out complete fighting technique from repairs enterprise and has made it available to those formations. It is clear now why he did expel the management of enterprise. In that area there is a belief that those are the only units capable to save the Serb people and Dunjic was declared to be the best Serb officer. Sir, at least from this paragraph would you agree that it sounds like you are less of a brigade commander and more of an organiser of the paramilitaries yourself? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: All right. And if we continue on, the next paragraph talks about the seriousness of the situation at Zuc in December, and as a result the command sent Kosovac, who is the author of this, and Lieutenant-Colonel Maljkovic to the area on the 8th to help in overhauling the situation. I'm going to move to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please provide a reference in the original in B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Yes. So we are on page 2 in both documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And it says: "Unsatisfied with a general situation and a danger for this part of the front, some municipality leaders, with the alleged approval by the Presidency, decided to arrest commands of Rajlovac and Vogosca Brigade, and the executor was Major Dunjic together with his men. Besides command of brigade, also Colonel Kosovac and Lieutenant-Colonel Maljkovic were arrested." Now, sir, you don't deny in September 1992 you were in the Zuc area and you made some arrests; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Well, I denied that I was at Zuc. I mean, I was below Zuc. Let us be precise. I was in Rajlovac. And it is correct that I arrested Colonel Kosovac and Lieutenant-Colonel Maljkovic, and it is correct that I arrested almost the entire municipality of Rajlovac. And I think that that was a brilliant move in order to save tens of thousands of the Serb people.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Let's speak specifically about who went along with you. This talks about your men. Were these men from Brne's unit who were with you?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Part of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I also understand that there were political figures with you as well, specifically Ratko Radic from the Ilijas municipality, and Trifko Radic as well. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Ratko Radic was president of the municipality of Hadzici, and he was not with me. Trifko Radic was not with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Who specifically gave the order for you to make these arrests?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Was there anyone above you who gave the order?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So were the one who originated this idea and made a decision to arrest other commanders of brigades?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Correct. I'm the one who made the decision and issued the order.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: It goes on to say: [As read] "During the arrest, the most severe methods were applied as it was about the most severe criminals. For arresting complete commands of brigade there was no justification because the arrested men were the persons who remained in the brigade until the last day. Instead to arrest those who ran away, they arrested the persons who remained. By this act their brigades remained without leaders in the moments of strongest offensive by the enemy. And the following day also the head of the corpus staff was exposed to mistreatment, Colonel Marcetic. And during these actions there were robberies and thefts of military property." Sir, do you deny that during this entire event that crimes were committed? Here robberies and thefts of military property.

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: It's not by accident that I asked you who it was that had signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, you can just give me a simple answer. Were any crimes committed? Were any thefts committed? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Thefts, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Any other crimes? Looting?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: I don't know because I was at the front line then. After these arrests I had to get the lines back, so I wasn't present there. I'm talking about the time after the arrest of these structures.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: The last paragraph, the last paragraph in the English: "That the Main Staff together with the Presidency of the Republika Srpska evaluates the situation, that the leadership states who support and who is behind all of this and then, on the basis of the political decision, start ... serious cleansing of para-authorities of para-army." It appears here that they are labelling you as a paramilitary. Do you disagree with that assessment?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Well, after all of this happened, a meeting was held in the municipality of Rajlovac that was attended by Mr. Krajisnik, Mrs. Plavsic, Mr. Mico Stanisic, Mr. Galic corps commander, and the presidents of municipalities, these six municipalities in the north-west. After my explanation with regard to the reasons for this arrest and everything that was implied by that, namely that we should keep the lines, I received the support of one and all then. Your Honours, may I -- may I just explain something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was the only professional person in the brigade and my logic was military logic, the logic of a soldier. If I arrest those who outrank me, who had sent false reports to the brigade command, I mean the -- the commander of the brigade and the Chief of Staff of the brigade who had fled from that brigade, by arresting them and by arresting part of the municipal leadership, this is what the soldiers would think. They would start wondering what lay in store for us, they would think if these people are being arrested, so that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, you just described this meeting and you indicated a number of people there including Mr. Galic, and you noted that at the end of the meeting you received the support of one and all of them. Are you suggesting that as a result of this meeting Mr. Galic then gave you his support?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: He didn't state his views, but the general conclusion of the meeting was the one that I've already stated.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. So that conclusion excludes the opinion of Mr. Galic then; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if that's correct. He didn't say anything. He was not explicit. He didn't explicitly say anything against that at that meeting. He didn't say anything explicitly against what I had done after I explained what I had done.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. We will get to that. But if you could just look at the B/C/S, please, and go to the very last paragraph, and I don't believe that this is in English. Would you mind reading out that very last paragraph in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Read it out loud. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: "Also we propose that Major Dunjic urgently be dismissed from his duties, be arrested, and to have criminal proceedings instituted against him because he overstepped his authority and because he disobeyed the corps command." This was signed by the man who I had arrested a day before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not sure in regard to the time. I suspect I have at least another 15 minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it's time for adjournment for today. Mr. Dunjic, we will adjourn for today and continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. Here at the Tribunal, we have a rule that the witness is not supposed to discuss with anybody else about his or her testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that, and I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 28th day of November, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.43 p.m.,
